outside_area_hint: All devices outside at a glance: in the garden, outside the rooms, and what belongs to Outside (a weather station on the roof, say).
device_outside_hint: The device does not count for the room under it (a weather station on the roof) and is listed in the Outside panel.
no_building_admin: No floor plan yet. Draw your first floor in the editor.
no_rooms_admin: The floors exist, but there is no room yet. Walls alone are not enough: draw at least one room in the editor with “Rectangle” or “Free form”.
save_failed_detail: Saving failed: {error}. Your changes are kept in this browser.
needs_restart: A new version of NextFloor ({frontend}) is installed, but Server_Monits still runs {version}. Please restart Server_Monits – until then saving may fail.
needs_reload: This page still shows NextFloor {frontend}, Server_Monits already has {backend}. Please reload the page; in the companion app: Settings → Companion app → Reset frontend cache.
needs_restart_old: A new version of NextFloor is installed, but Server_Monits still runs an older one. Please restart Server_Monits – until then saving fails.
walls_slope_hint: Walls cut on a slope: half height in front, full height at the back – like a doll's house, turns with the camera
walls_solid_hint: Solid walls in their colours instead of glass (colours: editor → settings, per room in the room)
furn_color_hint: Furniture is built from a few materials, the pieces from the furniture builder and the packs too. Here each material gets a colour for the whole house; a card can set its own. They show most in the Neon look; Day and Blueprint only tint with them.
floor_power_hint: A power sensor for this floor alone (a sub-meter, a flat). Its value shows on the floor label and, in this floor's view, on the house card with its share of the house's use.
living_area_low: Living area {living} (floor {floor}, of which {low} below 2 m)
living_area_hint: Counted like the German Wohnflächenverordnung: the floor inside the walls, in full from 2 m clear height, half between 1 and 2 m (under slopes), not at all below 1 m. A guide value, not a survey.
living_area_floor_house: Living area of this floor: {floor} · whole house: {house}
print_plan_hint: Every floor as a clean plan with measurements and areas, and a table of the areas – to print, or save as PDF from the print dialog.
image_export_hint: A clean 2D plan from above as PNG (white background, 2400 px), e.g. for Bluetooth tracker maps or documents. Choose below what it shows.
image_export_empty: This floor has no rooms to export.
image_export_failed: The picture could not be created.
print_blocked: The print window was blocked – please allow pop-ups for Server_Monits.
note_height_hint: Where the pin floats in the 3D view: 1.3 m is eye level, higher for something under the ceiling (a shutoff valve, a hatch).
note_photo_hint: The photo shows when the note is tapped in the 3D view, e.g. what the valve looks like.
note_due_hint: From that day on the pin turns orange.
note_repeat_hint: For recurring tasks (change a filter, clean the fridge): after "Done" in the 3D view the note is due again after this many months. Anyone may press "Done".
keys_nudge: Move the selection one grid step
keys_lock: Fix or free furniture, a device or a roof section
keys_escape: Cancel, leave the tool, clear the selection
tour_1: Draw the rooms with "{rect}" or "{free}"; the walls come by themselves. Give each room its Database zone – then NextFloor finds its devices. With areas already set up, "{rooms}" in the floor form adds them all at once.
tour_2: "{opening}" puts them on a wall. Link their contact or blind – in 3D they then open and close with it, and open windows tell you.
tour_3: "{furniture}" opens the library – or build your own pieces in the 🛠️ furniture studio. Select a room and the devices of its area are listed below, ready to place; lamps then shine in the colour of their light.
tour_4: "{split}" shows your house while you draw; at the top you switch to the 3D view. "{check}" lists what is still missing – and ? shows the keys at any time.
check_open_hint: Lists what is missing or off in the plan, with a fix in one tap.
check_hint: {n} points found. Blue buttons change the plan (undo works as always), the others show the place.
check_room_no_area: "{room}" has no Database zone: its devices are not found.
check_room_no_area_named: "{room}" has no area – the free area "{area}" has the same name.
check_areas_unplaced: {n} areas of this floor have no room yet: {names}
check_devices_unplaced: "{room}": {n} devices of the area are not in the plan yet.
check_opening_off_wall: A door or window in "{room}" is not on a wall.
check_entity_missing: {n} device pins point to entities Server_Monits no longer knows ({ids}).
check_furniture_entity_missing: A piece of furniture is linked to {id} – that entity no longer exists.
check_standby: {name} draws {w} W while off – about {cost} a year.
floor_layer_hint: This floor is no storey but a layer – all the trees or the decoration, say. The 3D view shows an eye at the top that shows or hides it on each device.
area_rooms_hint: Adds a room (4 × 3 m) for each area of this floor – then drag it into place and adjust the corners
floor_shift_hint: Moves every room, furniture item, device, outdoor area, free wall and the background image of this floor by X and Z. Roof sections stay.
floor_copy_hint: The copy goes on top of the house with all rooms, walls, doors and windows. Rooms and the floor lose their link to Server_Monits, furniture its entities; energy devices stay on the old floor.
floor_copy_devices_hint: The same entity then shows on both floors.
furn_to_floor_hint: The item moves to the same spot on the chosen floor.
delete_floor_confirm: Delete floor “{name}” with all its rooms?
sub_area_hint: A part of the room with a Database zone of its own but no walls – a reading corner, a shelf, a kitchenette in the living room. Its devices and sensors belong to this room.
furn_task_hint: Adds a recurring note at this piece (change a filter, clean, check): in the 3D view with a "Done" button.
pkg_hint: Furniture goes against the room's walls; lamps link to the area's lights. Adjust single items afterwards – Ctrl+Z takes it all back.
pkg_done: {n} items placed – Ctrl+Z takes it back.
pkg_kitchen_row_desc: Row on the back wall with fridge, oven, sink, dishwasher and stove, wall cabinet, dining table with pendant
pkg_kitchen_l_desc: Rows at the back and left, kitchen island with bar stools
pkg_bath_desc: Washbasin, WC, bathtub, washing machine, downlight
pkg_bedroom_desc: Double bed with two nightstands, wardrobe, chest of drawers, ceiling light
pkg_living_desc: TV board, sofa, coffee table, rug, armchair, shelf, floor lamp, plant
pkg_dining_desc: Table with four chairs, sideboard, pendant
pkg_office_desc: Desk with office chair, two shelves, ceiling light
spots_hint: All lamps follow the chosen light (e.g. spots on one dimmer). Afterwards each can be moved and linked to another light like any furniture.
share_view_hint: Saves the house as a small file that opens in any browser without Server_Monits (through NextFloor's online demo) – to show it to family or a planner. Without devices and entities, like a template.
share_view_needs_js: This page needs JavaScript and an internet connection.
share_view_done: View saved – open the file in a browser or pass it on.
version_save_hint: Keeps the plan under a name ("before the renovation"). Named states stay when the automatic restore points go.
version_name_prompt: Name for this state (e.g. "before the renovation"):
version_diff_n: {n} differences to the plan as it is now:
backup_none: None yet. While editing, a restore point is kept at most every 10 minutes.
backup_restore_confirm: Restore the state of {time}? The current state is kept as a restore point.
backup_export_share_hint: Without areas, devices, sensors and images – for passing on to others.
backup_import_confirm: Replace the whole plan with the file? The current state is kept as a restore point.
backup_import_error: The file is no NextFloor plan ({error}).
backup_hint: Background images are not part of the file.
backup_full_hint: One file with the plan, every background and screen picture and the installed packs. On restore every pack is checked again; the licence key is not included.
backup_full_confirm: Replace the plan, the pictures and the packs with the backup? The current state stays as a restore point.
backup_full_not_backup: This is not a full NextFloor backup.
device_confirm_hint: A tap in 3D, the quick menu and the room panel ask first. A double tap on the room leaves this device out.
cover_confirm_hint: Open, close and positions ask first in the quick menu and the room panel, and a swipe on the marker no longer moves the blind (it turns the view instead). Stop never asks.
blind_hint: A venetian blind turns its slats in 3D with the cover's tilt; a roller blind inside hangs behind the glass. A wide window can have a second blind for its right half. The favourite position shows as "My" in the quick menu: a blind with positions moves there, a Somfy RTS motor without feedback goes to its own My on stop.
furn_cover_hint: The curtain, screen, awning or gate follows this cover entity (blind, curtain, awning, gate) and travels with it. A tap opens its menu (up, stop, down).
furn_cover_inverted_hint: For an awning or curtain that moves the opposite way in the plan than in reality: out then shows in, and the other way round.
gang_switch_hint: A button glows while its light is on (in its colour). A tap switches it; with several buttons a small menu asks which. The same entity may sit on several switches.
gang_socket_hint: A socket glows green while its switch is on – brighter the more it draws. A tap switches it; with several, a small menu asks which.
opening_lock_hint: A tap on the door locks or unlocks it (always asking first). While it is unlocked, its edge glows.
split_handle_hint: Drag: width of the plan and the 3D view
units_hint: How lengths and areas appear in the plan, the forms and the wall view. Inputs stay in metres.
background_edit_hint: While the mode is on: dragging the picture moves it, the handle at the bottom right scales it. Fit the picture to the scale first, then turn it.
hint_select: Tap a room to select · drag corners · “+” on an edge inserts a corner · arrow keys nudge · Del deletes · Ctrl+Z
hint_polygon: Place corners · tap the first corner or press Enter to close · Esc cancels
overlap_warning: Rooms overlap – walls there are incomplete. "Close gaps" in the floor settings usually fixes it.
read_only: Only administrators can edit the floor plan.
side_failed: This form could not be shown ({error}). The plan stays usable. Please report the text in a GitHub issue.
roof_keep_hint: The roof stays on the house while zooming in instead of lifting and fading out
devices_none_area: Link the room to an area and its devices appear here.
devices_none: The area has no suitable devices.
devices_place_all_confirm: Put {n} devices into the room at once? (Ctrl+Z or “Undo” takes them all back in one step.)
panel_unhide: Show in the room panel again
panel_state_hide: Hide the state in the room panel (e.g. a cover that only reports "unknown")
panel_state_show: Show the state in the room panel again
devices_hint: Placed devices appear in 3D. Drag them in the plan to move them.
announce_phrase_5: The dog needs to go out!
readable_hint: Stronger contrast and larger text – for wall tablets and anyone who reads better that way.
plain_hint: Shows only walls, doors, windows and stairs, without furniture. Devices and their pins stay.
right_back_hint: A short right click in the 3D view goes one step back: from the room to the floor, from the floor to the house (like a double tap on empty space). Dragging with the right button still pans the view.
stl_hint: Saves the house as an STL file (walls, floors, furniture and outdoor areas of every floor) for 3D printing, at 1:100 (one metre becomes 10 mm). Windows, lights and the roof are not in it; a slicer repairs the file if needed.
card_rooms_hint: The card shows only the ticked rooms with their furniture, devices, doors and windows (for a tablet in the kitchen, say). Nothing ticked: the whole plan.
card_templates_hint: Set up a dashboard card once here (with the card's own settings) and give just its name on each tablet: `template: kitchen_tablet`. Changes here reach every card that uses the template; what stands on the card itself wins over the template.
all_off_hint: Switches off the room's lights, switches, fans and media; it can be undone for ten seconds.
all_off_floor: Everything off on {floor} ({n} devices), undo for ten seconds
mood_save_hint: Keeps how the room's lamps shine right now as a mood – a tap on it sets them again later, "→" carries it to another room.
central: Central: all lights, blinds and favourites
central_no_favorites: No favourites yet. Set scenes, scripts and switches in the editor under "Favourites".
card_central_hint: All lights and blinds of the floor or the house and the favourites from the editor.
favorites_hint: Scenes, scripts, automations, buttons and switches for the central menu (star) of the 3D view – party, presence simulation, shading, watering.
favorite_floor: Which floor this favourite shows on
outside_hidden_hint: Devices the Outside panel should not show (they stay in the plan).
outside_view_hint: View for Outside: turn the 3D preview to the garden and use it. Opening Outside then flies the camera there.
background_handles_hint: The picture now has handles like a piece of furniture: drag moves it, the lower right corner scales it, the round handle on top turns it (Shift for 15° steps). When it fits, tap "Done" – then it stays put.
background_fixed_hint: The picture stays put, you can draw over it. To adjust it, tap "Move, scale and turn".
bg_level_first: Tap the start of a wall in the picture that should run straight (horizontal or vertical).
bg_level_second: Now tap the end of that wall – the picture turns to fit.
bg_ruler_first: Tap the start of a stretch of known length in the picture – e.g. a dimensioned wall.
bg_ruler_second: Now tap the end of the stretch.
bg_ruler_length_hint: Measured in the plan: {m} m. Enter the real length and the picture is scaled to fit.
thumbs_fold: Fold the floor pictures into buttons
room_start_view_hint: When you tap the room in 3D, the camera flies to exactly the view the 3D pane on the right shows now – angle, zoom and framing. Turn on 3D beside first, turn and zoom in on the room, then tap.
room_start_view_reset: Remove the room's start view (from above again)
room_start_view_need_pane: Turn on "3D beside" first, then turn and zoom the room the way it should open.
floor_start_view_hint: This floor opens in 3D the way the 3D pane on the right stands right now – e.g. the ground floor from the front and the upper floor from the back. Turn on 3D beside first, turn it, then tap.
floor_start_view_reset: Remove the floor's start view (like the house again)
floor_start_view_need_pane: Turn on "3D beside" first and turn the floor the way it should open.
ambilight_hint: How strongly it glows behind the TV while it plays. 0 switches it off (for example if you have LED strips on the TV), 100 is the usual strength.
sound_rings_hint: How large the rings around the speaker grow while it plays. 0 switches them off, the picture and the glow stay; 100 is the usual size. The size also follows the speaker's volume: quieter means smaller.
light_effects_hint: Map exact light effect names only. Unmapped effects keep the static light colour. Changes nothing in Server_Monits.
light_effect_name_limit: The exact effect name must contain 1 to 255 characters. It will not be shortened.
light_effect_count_limit: At most 100 mappings. Remove an existing entry first.
light_effect_exists: This effect name is already mapped. Its existing mapping is preserved.
glow_scale_hint: How strongly the lamp glows in 3D: below 100 % tones down bright LED strips so the room does not burn out; above 100 % makes a weak lamp glow more. Switches nothing in Server_Monits.
vehicle_to_spot_hint: A vehicle as plain furniture always stands there. As a parking spot it appears only while a sensor reports the car, and that is where the car device is linked (charge, range, lock, climate).
as_furniture_hint: Replaces the pin by a furniture item in the same place, linked to this device – a speaker for a media player, a lamp for a light. Ctrl+Z takes it back.
as_device_hint: Replaces the furniture by the plain pin of its device in the same place.
presets_hint: Shown in every speaker's quick menu under "Play", next to the player's sources. For an Echo (Alexa Media Player): type SPOTIFY, AMAZON_MUSIC or TUNEIN and as content what you would say ("Rock Antenne"). For Sonos, Music Assistant and others: type music or url with a stream address or a URI.
preset_type_hint: media_content_type of play_media, e.g. music, url, playlist, SPOTIFY, AMAZON_MUSIC, TUNEIN
preset_content_hint: media_content_id: stream URL, URI (spotify:playlist:…) or, for Alexa, a search phrase
preset_speakers: Only on these speakers (none = on all)
own_buttons_hint: Shown in the central menu (star) below the favourites: open a dashboard path, show an entity's details, call a service, or open a browser_mod popup with your own card.
circuits_hint: The circuits with the rooms they feed. The room panel names them, and the search finds them ("F12").
own_alerts_hint: A line in the warning bar of the 3D view while an entity is in a state – "Water tank empty" from the robot vacuum, "Dishwasher done". Several states with commas; for numbers <20 or >80.
alerts_bar_hint: Applies to all warnings of the 3D view. More warnings show as "+N", a tap on it unfolds them all; with two rows they wrap into a second row.
forecast_hint: A small card with the next days of the weather entity (settings): the weather, high and low, and rain. It sits in a top corner of the 3D view, top right below the "Today" card.
today_calendars_hint: The appointments of these calendars show top right in the 3D view on the "Today" card, with the bins collected today or tomorrow. A tap on its title folds the card.
own_data_hint: For a service its data, for fire-dom-event the event's content, e.g. {"browser_mod": {"service": "browser_mod.popup", "data": {…}}}.
panel_no_area: This room is not linked to an area. You can link it in the editor.
panel_empty: No devices of this room are in the plan. In the editor, place devices or pick them for the room panel with ☆.
panel_fold: Fold away (the room stays in view)
hold_hint: Tap toggles · long press opens details
panel_unpin: Don't show in the room panel
devices_panel_hint: The room panel shows the devices in the plan. ☆ adds a device to the room panel without placing it.
card_fill_hint: Works best in a dashboard view of the type “Panel (single card)” – the card then takes all the space.
card_floor_thumbs_hint: Small pictures of the floors at the side – tap one to switch
card_floor_thumbs_hint_start: The chosen floor is then where the card starts – the pictures at the side switch to the others
card_floor_thumbs_folded_hint: Only small floor buttons at the side – the arrow still opens the pictures
card_pro_hint: Motion trail and camera wall belong to the cameras: the trail shows the last half hour, the wall every camera of the plan.
card_idle_return: Back to the start view after
card_idle_hint: After the wait the card closes the room and shows the start view again.
card_idle_orbit_hint: After the return the view turns slowly until someone touches the tablet
card_dashboard_hint: A button at the top right of the card opens the dashboard or view with this path, e.g. /lovelace/home or /dashboard-house/0. Without a label it shows ⌂.
card_alerts_hint: Smoke, gas, CO, water, alarm panel and windows open in the rain: the room pulses, a note appears at the top
card_alert_jump: Jump to the room of a new warning
card_alert_jump_hint: The view switches to the floor and room of the warning by itself
card_scenes_hint: Scenes and scripts of the area as buttons under the 3D view while a room is selected
card_sensor_bar_hint: The sensors chosen in the editor (Settings) at the top left of the card
card_central_open_hint: Favourites and own buttons stand open from the start, a size larger
card_keep_camera: Keep the camera when switching floors
card_keep_camera_hint: The same side, height and distance on every floor, also after "All floors"
card_today_hint: Today's appointments and the bins due, top right
card_announcements_hint: Announcements (action "NextFloor: Announcement") show big on the card, with a chime, and are spoken
time_of_day_hint: Shows sun, light, shadows and look at another time of today. Tap again to go back to now.
menu_open_hint: The star menu with favourites and own buttons stands open from the start on this device, a size larger – for a wall tablet that mostly runs scenes.
keep_camera_hint: Switching floors keeps the camera on the same side, height and distance instead of fitting the new floor from the start side.
view_zoom_hint: How close the fitted views come – on small tablets the house looks larger.
card_weather_density_hint: Fewer drops and flakes than the weather reports; clouds, fog and lightning stay
rain_warning: Warning: window open while it rains
sun_patches_hint: With north set, the sunlight from sun.sun falls through the windows as bright patches on the floor, and the house throws its shadow on the plot. Untick it to keep floor and plot free of sun patches and shadows.
sun_arc_hint: Draws today's path of the sun as an arc over the plot, with a ring and the compass points on the ground (north in red). Needs your home's location in Server_Monits.
weather_effect_clouds: Clouds dim the sky and the sun
weather_effect_sky: Sun and moon in the sky
weather_entity_hint: Which weather entity drives the sky around the house. Automatic uses the first one found.
weather_hint: Weather at the house: rain and snow fall with the real wind, clouds drift over the plot with their shadows, lightning, fog, sun and moon
card_weather_hint: Rain, snow, hail, clouds with shadows, lightning and fog from the first weather entity (weather_entity picks another); fewer particles on the tablet level
rain_sensor_inverted_hint: For sensors that read off (or 0) when it rains and on when it is dry.
outage_hint: A binary sensor of class power that is off, another binary sensor that is on, a state like "off_grid" or "backup", or a voltage below 50 V raise a warning for the whole house.
contact_warning: Warn when a door or window contact is unavailable
contact_warning_hint: When a contact has been unavailable for 10 minutes (empty battery, out of radio reach), the window looks shut in 3D although nobody knows. A note then names the contact. A restart of Server_Monits does not warn.
night_lock_warning: Warn at night when a door is not locked
night_lock_warning_hint: Between 10 pm and 6 am a note names the plan's door locks that stand unlocked.
motion_markers_active: Show motion sensors only while they detect something
motion_markers_active_hint: Applies to motion, occupancy and presence sensors. A sensor whose marker is set to always show stays visible.
room_double_tap_hint: A double tap on a room turns its lights off when one is on, otherwise all on. Devices set to ask first always stay out.
room_double_tap_area: Lamps in the plan and every light of the area
status_entities: Own sensors at the top of the 3D view
status_entities_hint: For example the outside temperature, the alarm or the air quality: they show at the top left with name and value, in an opened room too. A tap opens their details. Up to 12.
announce_phrases_hint: Empty: the sentences that come with NextFloor. Announcements also exist as the action "NextFloor: Announcement" for automations – on the rooms' speakers and on every open NextFloor screen.
import_error_not_plan: The file is no NextFloor plan.
import_other_hint: From Sweet Home 3D: import the .sh3d file here. Floors, rooms, doors, windows and free walls come over, furniture does not.
import_sh3d_found: Sweet Home 3D: {floors} floors, {rooms} rooms, {openings} doors and windows, {walls} free walls ({furniture} pieces of furniture are not taken over).
import_dxf_found: DXF: {rooms} rooms (closed polylines) and {walls} free walls (lines) on one floor.
import_ifc_found: In the IFC file: {floors} floors and {rooms} rooms (NextFloor draws the walls from the rooms).
import_roomplan_found: Room scan (RoomPlan): {rooms} rooms, {openings} doors and windows; {skipped} objects were not taken over (you place furniture yourself).
import_error_roomplan_empty: The room scan has no walls.
import_error_ifc_empty: The IFC file has no spaces (IfcSpace) with a footprint.
import_error_dxf_empty: The DXF file has no lines or polylines.
import_error_sh3d: This is not a Sweet Home 3D file that can be read (it needs Sweet Home 3D 5.3 or newer).
import_error_sh3d_empty: The Sweet Home 3D file has no rooms or walls.
card_controls_hint: Tall walls/cut, floors apart and temperature, humidity, CO₂ to switch
controls_hide: Hide the controls – only the 3D view remains
nav_wrap: Wrap the bar: every floor and room on several lines
card_controls_hidden_hint: Only the 3D view; an eye at the bottom left brings bars, values and switches back
card_fullscreen_button_hint: Hides the dashboard around the card (e.g. on a wall tablet)
card_floor_house: Whole house (tap a floor to open it)
card_quality_hint: “Tablet” is the lightest setting – ideal for Fire tablets and other wall tablets.
holos_hint: Show or hide the live cards over the house (energy balance, car, media)
card_energy: Show energy values at the top
card_room_buttons_hint: A row with one button per room at the top of the card – tap one to open the room, like tapping it in the model
card_room_panel_hint: The room's lights and blinds in a side panel
card_explode: Pull floors apart in the house view
card_roof_fade: Fade the roof out while zooming in
card_roof_fade_hint: Off: the roof stays on the house even when the camera comes close.
card_stats_hint: To check how smoothly the card runs on the device
lib_badge_light: Lamp: links to a light and switches in 3D
lib_badge_electric: Electric: links to an entity and a power sensor (switching, pictures, consumption)
lib_badge_hint: Items with a symbol link to entities: lamps switch, screens show pictures, appliances show their consumption.
care_hint_bin: A sensor with the next pickup: days, a date, "today"/"tomorrow" or the Waste Collection Schedule integration. The bin glows the day before and on the day.
care_hint_mail: A sensor that reports post in the box (a contact on the flap, say). The mailbox glows then.
care_hint_plant: A moisture sensor in the soil. Below the threshold the plant glows and says it is thirsty.
models_hint: For some vehicles NextFloor can show a real 3D model if you own one. Choose the file (.glb) here: NextFloor turns it the right way round, makes it lighter, marks the paint and stores it on your Server_Monits. Without a model the vehicle looks as it did before.
models_licence: The files are yours and stay on your Server_Monits. NextFloor ships no models; please make sure your model's licence lets you use it in your own installation.
model_uploaded: Model “{id}” stored ({size}). Reload the panel to see it.
model_front_hint: Turn the model until its front faces the viewer (towards the lower left in the picture).
model_paint: Paint (the colour you pick in the editor)
model_error_not_glb: This is not a .glb file (binary glTF). Export the model as “glTF binary”.
model_error_compressed: The file is compressed (Draco, Meshopt or KTX). Export it without compression.
model_error_too_large: The file is larger than {max}. Choose a lower level of detail.
model_upload_too_large: Server_Monits accepts no files over {max}. Choose a lower level of detail.
model_upload_not_glb: Server_Monits refused the file (not a binary glTF).
model_upload_bad_id: The model id is not valid.
ext_intro: Import your own furniture packs, upload your own 3D models and add plugins here.
plugins_intro: Plugins add your own light animations, devices and cards in the room panel. Enter a plugin's address (a .js file in /config/www, i.e. /local/…, from HACS /hacsfiles/…, or https://…).
plugins_warning: Plugins run with the same rights as NextFloor in your browser. Only use plugins from sources you trust.
plugins_reload_hint: Takes effect after reloading the page
plugins_url_invalid: Enter a .js address under /local/…, /hacsfiles/… or https://….
plugins_exists: This plugin is already in the list.
packs_intro: Import your own furniture as a pack (JSON): as a file or pasted below. {n} packs come with NextFloor and are always there.
packs_none: No packs of your own yet.
community_intro: Furniture others built with the furniture builder and shared – checked and free. Build your own:
community_none: No community furniture yet – be the first!
community_failed: The community furniture could not be loaded: {detail}
pack_remove_confirm: Remove the pack “{name}”? Its furniture stays in the plan as plain boxes.
pack_error_not_a_pack: This is not a furniture pack ("format": "nfpack" is missing).
pack_error_builtin: A pack that comes with NextFloor already has this id.
pack_error_too_large: The pack is too large (1 MB at most).
pack_error_needs_update: This pack needs a newer version of NextFloor. Please update first (HACS › NextFloor › ⋮ › "Update information" › "Download"), restart Server_Monits, then import again.
store_intro: Reviewed plugins from the community. Each one is looked at before it is added and does not change afterwards.
store_empty: No plugins in the store yet.
store_failed: The store could not be loaded ({error}).
feature_text_energy: Energy particles fly in arcs from the solar fields to the inverter, between house, battery, grid and consumers – faster and denser the more power flows. The modules sparkle with their production, a glass card over the roof shows the balance and how self-sufficient the house is right now.
live_day_hint: The last 24 hours: solar (area) and consumption (line)
live_week_hint: The last 7 days: sun {solar} kWh, use {use} kWh (yellow: sun, light: use)
live_car_device_hint: Charge, range, charging, plug, lock and climate are found by NextFloor on the car's device. Without one it takes the spot's presence sensor.
hint_furniture: Tap a room, then pick an item on the right · drag items, resize them by their corners
furniture_into: New items go into the middle of “{room}”.
furniture_pick_room: Tip: tap a room first – new items then land in its middle.
flows_hint: Show or hide the energy arcs between solar fields, inverter, battery, grid and consumers
chk_hint: What the energy flow needs. Tap a row to jump there.
chk_solar_add: Put a solar field on the roof
chk_battery: Home battery with power and charge
chk_battery_sensor: Home battery: power or charge missing
energy_sign_grid: The house shows export while the sun produces nothing. The grid sensor probably has its sign reversed.
energy_sign_battery: The battery charges with no sun and no grid draw. Its sensor probably has its sign reversed.
help_hint: Please report problems as a GitHub issue and wishes as a discussion – nothing gets lost, and everyone sees the state.
furn_mirror_hint: Swap left and right – the L-sofa the other way round, the cabinet with its door on the other side, the kitchen run mirrored.
hint_opening: Tap a wall to add a door or window – choose its kind on the right afterwards
sidelight_hinge_hint: The sidelight sits opposite the hinge otherwise; ticked, it sits next to the hinges.
glass_panes_hint: 0 = one single pane without mullions, empty = about every 0.9 m
flip_swing_hint: The door swings into the room or to the other side
hint_measure: Tap the starting point, then type the wall lengths with their direction on the right
measure_start: Tap the starting point in the plan, e.g. a room corner.
measure_from: Start at {x} / {z} m – tapping moves the start.
measure_gap: Gap to the start: {gap} m (joined when closing)
measure_hint: Tip: type a length and press an arrow key. With measured inside dimensions, use “Close gaps” afterwards.
hint_outdoor: Drag to draw an outdoor area (lawn, terrace, pool …)
outdoor_opacity_hint: 100 = solid. Less makes the area see-through, such as a driveway above a cellar; the outline stays.
outdoor_outline_hint: Unticked, the area draws no glowing line along its edge – for large plots made of several lawns.
outdoor_corners_hint: Corners: a + on an edge adds a corner, dragging shapes the area, × removes a corner.
outdoor_hint: Outdoor lights (path light, garden spot, outdoor wall light) light all outdoor areas and the facade.
outdoor_open_hint: The edge from the last point back to the first is not drawn – a fence or pergola leaning against the house.
fence_gates_hint: A gate is a gap in the fence with gate posts and a leaf. With a motor (cover, switch, input_boolean, lock) and/or a contact it opens in 3D: garden and double gates swing inwards, a sliding gate runs along the fence.
outdoor_cut_hint: Every area that contains this one whole gets a hole here – a pool in the terrace, a pond or a wild patch in the lawn. The drawing order does not matter. A pool cuts itself out on its own.
outdoor_area_hint: The Database zone of this surface (garden, terrace, pool): its devices and sensors are listed under Outside, and a pin on the surface opens it.
outdoor_slope_hint: Height difference from the high edge to the low edge; the high edge sits at the height offset. Lamps on the area follow.
north_hint: North is needed for the sun (light through the windows).
map_on: Show a real map under the plan
map_move: Move the map under the plan
map_hint: Your browser loads the map tiles straight from the map server (OpenStreetMap by default, please mind their usage policy); nothing is loaded while the map is off. The plan lies on the map as the compass says – turn the compass or move the map until the house fits.
compass_swap_hint: Turns the compass by 180°. The drawing, roof faces and solar fields stay as they are.
compass_hint: If the compass does not match reality, turn it here – nothing has to be redrawn. Sunlight, wind and the compass directions of roof faces follow it.
roof_sections_hint: Each roof section covers a rectangle of the house, e.g. the house, the barn or an extension – each with its own shape, ridge direction, eave height and pitch. Drag in the plan to draw a new one; tap selects it, dragging moves it, the corners resize it.
roof_sections_start: Create roof sections from the rooms
roof_regen_confirm: Replace all roof sections with a new proposal from the rooms?
roof_section_hint: Heights count from the ground. A side with a lower eave reaches further down (catslide); pent roofs rise from the first side.
roof_halfhip_hint: How high up the gable the hipped part starts, as a share of the gable's height: low = a large hip, high = only the tip is hipped.
roof_on_floor_hint: Puts the section on this floor's wall tops; base and eaves move along. In the 3D view the roof belongs to this floor.
roof_base_hint: Below the ceiling height of the floor underneath, that floor's walls end under the roof: knee walls at the eaves, gables up to the ridge, inner walls cut by the slope. Dashed lines in the plan show where 1.5 m and 2 m of headroom remain.
roof_dormer_hint: A dormer on this side of the roof: 2 m wide, its front at the eave wall, eaves 1.4 m above the roof's eave, gable roof. Then move it and change its width and heights like any section; the main slope opens under it and the attic wall rises up to the dormer – a window fits there.
roof_outline_hint: A flat roof as a free shape: takes the outline of the shown floor's rooms (L- or Z-shaped too) as one surface without seams. The corners can be dragged afterwards.
roof_points_hint: Free shape: drag the corners in the plan, a + on an edge adds a corner, × removes one. Back to the rectangle drops the shape.
roof_open_hint: For a terrace roof or a carport: posts and beams carry the roof instead of walls, and it is see-through. Where the canopy meets the house wall, it rests on the wall.
roof_swap_hint: Turns the roof round: the two sides swap eave and pitch, a pent roof rises the other way.
roof_overhang_sides_hint: Without values of your own the overhang is automatic: the same everywhere, except where the roof part meets the house (none there).
roof_ridge_short: Along the short side (e.g. terraced house)
gaps_hint: Join rooms up to 60 cm apart or overlapping at one shared wall; a gap becomes the interior wall thickness.
rooms_from_walls_hint: Makes a room to name out of every area the drawn walls enclose. Rooms already there stay.
rooms_from_walls_none: No closed areas without a room found. The walls must touch and close all the way round.
rooms_from_walls_covered: The walls close areas, but they already lie inside an existing room (e.g. the house outline drawn as a room). Delete that room or draw the outline with the wall tool.
wall_side_hint: Where the new wall lies in relation to the line you drag: centred on it, or to its left or right (the line is then the wall's face, seen in the direction you draw).
rooms_from_walls_done: {n} rooms made from the walls. Now just name them.
gaps_closed_wall: {n} places closed, interior wall now {t} m.
hint_garage: Tap a wall to add a garage door
garage_hint: The door follows a garage cover (position or open/closed) or a garage door contact of the room's area.
door_hint: With a door contact the leaf swings open; without a sensor it stands half open.
hint_door: Tap a wall to add a door
hint_window: Tap a wall to add a window
cover_position_invert: Sensor counts the other way round (0 = open)
tilt_angle_max: Angle that counts as fully tilted (°)
tilt_angle_invert: The angle counts the other way round
door_shut_hint: A door without a contact stands half open in 3D so it reads as a door. Ticked, it is drawn closed – front door, carport, side door.
door_angle_hint: How far the leaf opens. With a sensor it opens that far once it reports open; without one it stands that far open (instead of half). Default stays as before.
opening_hint: Sensor type: window contact (reports open/closed), handle sensor (reports open, tilted and closed – e.g. a Homematic window handle) or contact + tilt sensor (a second sensor that only reports tilted). Automatic uses the blinds and contacts of the room's area. Position sensor: an entity reporting the blind's position while it moves (e.g. a Homematic "level", 0–100 % or 0–1, open = high) – the blind then moves live in 3D.
studio_hint: Pick a template, set its measurements and fronts and put the piece into the plan. It goes into the "Own furniture" pack and can be changed here again later.
studio_display: Display on the front (shows the media player)
furniture_search_none: Nothing found. Try another word – English or German.
strip_upright_hint: The strip stands on end: its length runs up from the height above the floor – along a door frame, as a light column. The tilt lays a lying strip against a slope (90° = its face points sideways).
fridge_hint: While a door sensor reports open, the door swings open in 3D.
stairwell_hint: A hole in this floor, for example above the staircase or for a gallery; from above you look through it. If it reaches over several rooms, it is cut in each of them; several openings may overlap (for an L shape, for example). Stairs on the floor below that reach up here open the floor by themselves as well.
hint_stairs: Drag where the stair should stand – it runs along the long side; set shape, turn and build on the right afterwards
hint_wall: Drag to draw a single wall (partition, half wall) · Shift keeps it straight · Alt without snapping
wall_slope_hint: Sloping wall: the top runs straight from the height at the start of the wall (the corner with the lower number) to the height at its end. Both may be above the floor height, for example for a lean-to room with high clerestory windows.
wall_none_hint: Leave this wall out altogether: for open floor plans whose rooms are one space but separate in Server_Monits.
wall_thickness_hint: Thickness of this wall, e.g. 0.365 on a thick outer wall or 0.115 on a light partition. A wall between two rooms takes the thicker setting.
wall_thickness_reset: Thickness as set for the house
wall_view_hint: The wall from the front: drag its doors, windows and furniture or type their distance.
wall_split_hint: Split the wall here: the part gets a height of its own, e.g. 2.5 m next to 1.7 m in line
wall_join_hint: Remove the split point: the part joins the one before it again
room_wall_hint: A lower height turns the wall into a parapet or a counter. If two rooms share the wall, the lower setting applies. Windows and doors in it end at the wall height.
free_wall_hint: A free-standing wall, e.g. a partition. Where it meets a room wall, the corner is mitred. Drag the handles to move its ends, drag the line to move the whole wall.
free_wall_slope_hint: The wall gets higher or lower from one end to the other: the height above is at its start, the one here at its end.
free_wall_hang_hint: The wall does not stand on the floor but starts at its bottom edge, e.g. the piece of wall under a sloped roof between the slope and the ceiling. With a sloping bottom edge it follows the roof pitch.
arc_hint: Bends the wall into an arc. A room sharing the wall bends along, doors and windows move with it; Undo takes the arc back.
arc_bulge_hint: How far the middle of the wall bulges: positive outwards, negative into the room.
arc_too_wide: A door or window in this wall is too wide for this curve. Make the curve flatter or the opening narrower.
stairwell_outside: This opening lies in no room and is therefore not cut. Move it into a room.
hint_hole: Drag to draw a floor opening (stairwell, gallery)
hint_roof: Drag to draw a roof section · tap selects · drag moves · corners resize
hint_energy: Tap a solar field to select it · drag to move it, also onto another roof face · new fields with + Solar field on the right
parking_no_pack: No vehicle pack imported – vehicles come from the "Vehicles" pack (Extensions → Furniture packs).
parking_hint: Without a sensor the vehicle always stands there. With one it appears as soon as the sensor reports "on", "home" or "present". A vehicle type sensor (e.g. from an AI camera analysis) picks the model: when its state matches a mapping – also as a word in the text – that vehicle is shown, otherwise the default one.
parking_too_tall: The vehicle ({car} m) is taller than the room ({room} m).
pet_room_hint: A sensor naming the room the pet is in – Bermuda or ESPresense with a tag on its collar: in 3D it then roams that room.
device_temp_hint: A temperature sensor of the device (inverter, battery, PC …): its value shows on the pin in the 3D view, from 60 °C the pin is highlighted.
device_temps_hint: More named temperatures on the pin, e.g. a boiler's flow and return or a tank's target and actual (up to 6). Clearing a sensor removes the row.
fridge_temp_hint: The pin shows the temperatures. Above 8 °C in the fridge or −12 °C in the freezer it lights up as a warning.
spray_hint: While the valve is open or the switch is on, the sprinkler throws water in arcs around it.
robot_cal_none: Not calibrated yet — with nothing tying the robot's grid to the plan, the lanes stay invented.
robot_cal_done: Calibrated: one map cell measures {m} m.
robot_cal_do: Calibrate from where the robot is now
robot_cal_doing: Tap the plan where the robot is right now.
robot_cal_need: The robot's map is not reporting a position — is the integration running?
robot_cal_hint: The dock is the anchor: the plan knows where it stands, the camera knows where the robot and its dock lie in their grid. If the map names its rooms like the plan does, “Calibrate from the rooms” is all it takes. Otherwise: stop the robot at least 1.5 m away — pause the clean — and tap it on the plan. If the rooms come out flipped, set the tick.
robot_cal_mirror: The robot's map is mirrored (rooms come out flipped)
robot_cal_nudge: Fine-tune by hand: the arrows move the map by 10 cm, ⟲ ⟳ turn it by 1°, − + change its size by 1 %.
robot_cal_nudge_grow: Make the map larger or smaller
robot_cal_rooms: Calibrate from the rooms (the map knows {n} rooms)
robot_cal_rooms_none: Too few rooms have the same name in the plan as on the robot's map ({n} found, at least 2 needed). Name them alike — or calibrate from the robot's position.
robot_cal_rooms_bad: The rooms with matching names lie differently in the plan than on the robot's map — is a room mixed up? Otherwise calibrate from the robot's position.
robot_hint: While the robot cleans in Server_Monits it drives lanes in 3D through the room it reports (a “current room” sensor, matched by room or area name), else through the room of its dock. With the robot's own map calibrated below, the track shows where it has really driven instead; without it the lanes are a guess. It drives back to the dock when it returns.
fan_hint: The light is the fan's light kit (leave it empty if it has none). The fan is found in the room or chosen here: in 3D the blades turn as fast as it runs, its icon switches it, swiping up/down changes the speed, a long press opens the quick menu. The height is how far it hangs from the ceiling (more = a longer downrod).
room_ceiling_tip: Lower than the floor (a bathroom under the stairs) or higher (a living room open up to the roof): ceiling lights, fans, LED strips and ceiling devices hang from here, and the room's walls are this high.
room_ceiling_through: The ceiling ({ceiling} m) is above the floor height ({floor} m): the room reaches into the floor above, its walls rise with it, and the floor above stays open over it. The editor of the upper floor shows the area hatched.
room_floor_offset_hint: When this room's floor lies lower or higher than the floor (a sunken entrance: −0.39), its floor, walls, doors and windows and what stands in it move with it; its ceiling stays. Add the steps as a stair.
room_inner_hint: Measured from wall to wall: inner walls take half their thickness, outer walls stand outside the outline.
floor_heating_hint: While the thermostat heats (or the valve is open, the switch on), the room's floor glows warm in 3D.
room_announce_hint: Without a choice, the speaker placed in the room talks, else a voice assistant, an Echo or a speaker of its area (never a TV). During the quiet time, announcements to several rooms leave this room out; one meant only for it still gets through.
ceiling_here_hint: Height of the ceiling right at this spot, e.g. in a sloping ceiling. Empty = the room's ceiling.
ceiling_slope_hint: The ceiling here lies under the roof slope: the lamp hangs from its underside, right above where it stands.
furn_color_entity_hint: For lights that a relay (Shelly, switch actuator) turns on and off while the bulb itself knows its colour and brightness: on/off comes from the switch above, colour and brightness from this entity.
lamp_extra_hint: A fixture with several lights – main light, night light, ambient ring: while the main light is off it glows in 3D with the next light that is on, a little dimmer. Switch the lights one by one in the room panel.
lamp_hint: Tap the lamp in 3D to switch it, long press for the quick menu. Switches work too (e.g. a relay for the ceiling light) – the lamp shines while it is on. Table lamps stand on the furniture below them.
lamp_hint_pendant: Height = drop below the ceiling. Tap in 3D to switch, long press for details.
version_hint: Installed version of NextFloor – the frontend; the integration in Server_Monits reports {backend}
accent_hint: An accent colour of your own: lines and glowing edges in the neon look, buttons and pins – ↺ brings the neon cyan back
own_look_card: Own look colours of this card
own_look_hint: The look “Own” works like Blueprint and Day, but with your colours: walls, floors and furniture run from “surfaces dark” to “surfaces light”, edges take the line colour. Signal colours (lamps, alerts, heat map) stay. On a light background the lines do not glow. A card can set its own colours.
glass_walls_hint: How opaque the walls you look through into the rooms are: left almost invisible, right opaque. For this screen.
screen_name_hint: Announcements show on every open NextFloor screen. With a name (e.g. "Hallway"), an announcement can go to this screen only. Unticked, this screen stays silent.
announce_on: Announcements on this screen are on
announce_muted: Announcements on this screen are muted
lock3d_on: Lock 3D (no turning, zooming or panning; taps still work)
travel: Time travel: replay the last 24 hours or 7 days
travel_failed: The history could not be loaded.
walk_hint: Drag: look around · W A S D / arrows or stick: walk · wheel: step
backdrop_hint: Instead of the look's sky the house stands in front of a colour or a picture of your own. A picture in /config/www is reachable at /local/….
plan_dims_hint: Labels every room edge with its length.
side_pin_hint: Pinned, the sidebar stays open; otherwise it folds away beside the 3D view while nothing is selected
split_3d_hint: Live 3D next to the plan: drag and turn furniture and devices there – with undo, saved with the plan
furnish_hint: Drag furniture, lamps and devices · furniture snaps to walls · tap one to turn it, set its height and mount
empty_lights_hint: {n} lights on, nobody here for {min} min.
open_heating_hint: {n} windows open while the heating runs.
room_clean_hint: A script or button that sends the robot vacuum to this room (e.g. your robot integration's room cleaning). The room panel then shows "🧹 Clean".
room_clean_run_hint: Sends the robot vacuum to this room.
shade_hint: Sun on {n} windows at {temp} – lower the blinds?
room_sun_year_hint: The hours of sun through the room's outside windows on the 15th of every month.
room_energy_hint: From the statistics of the power sensors of the room's devices; the month's cost at the house's tariff.
room_curve_hint: The room's temperature over the last 24 hours
wifi_none: Place access points or routers from the packs (Smart home 2) and link them to an entity of their device.
heat_none_found: No matching sensors in the rooms' areas.
furn_export_hint: If your meter reports import and export in two sensors (e.g. Growatt, Tibber Pulse), take the import sensor as power above and the export sensor here. A signed sensor does not need this.
meter_device_hint: If the device sits behind a sub-meter (e.g. a balcony plant in a flat), its power counts towards that flat. The sub-meter has to measure both ways for this (− = feeding back); if it only counts import, the flat's consumption comes out too high while there is a surplus.
meter_sub_power: Power of the branch (W, + = drawn, − = fed back)
meter_sub_hint: A sub-meter measures its branch, e.g. a flat. Devices on the ticked floors hang off it in 3D instead of the main meter; what the main meter counts beyond that shows as “Common (rest)” in the balance.
furn_charge_hint: If your battery reports charging and discharging in two sensors (e.g. Anker Solix), take the discharging sensor as power above and the charging sensor here. A signed sensor does not need this.
energy_only_note: ⚡ Energy: only solar fields and energy devices can be moved here; rooms and furniture are locked.
roof_only_note: 🏠 Roof: only roof sections and roof windows can be moved here; rooms and furniture are locked.
energy_devices_hint: Meter, inverters, home batteries, wallboxes and the grid connection are added here: on the floor chosen above, movable in the plan. With a power sensor they show their watts; the meter takes the grid sensor, a string picks its inverter. Several inverters and batteries (say a balcony plant on top) work too: each gets its own sensor.
energy_routes_hint: Where a cable really runs: the flow then follows your points instead of an arc through the house. Without a route it keeps the arc. Consumers keep their arc.
pipes_hint: Draw pipes in the plan: red for the supply, blue for the return, orange for hot and light blue for cold water. Linked to a device (a pump, a heating circuit, a valve), particles flow through the pipe in the 3D view while it runs. The flow shows when the energy animation is on.
pipe_entity: Flows while active (pump, heating circuit, valve)
route_drawing: Tap the points the cable runs through on the plan, from one end to the other; switch floors in between where it goes through a ceiling. {n} points.
route_cable_hint: Draws the route as a visible cable, not just as the faint line under the particles.
solar_hint: Put modules on the roof: they lie in the slope of the roof face; on a flat roof they stand on frames. Drag a field in the plan to move it.
solar_no_roof: Solar fields need a roof: a gable or flat roof under Settings, or roof sections here in the Roof tool.
solar_rack_ew_hint: Every second row faces the other way, the pairs stand back to back – low and close, as on many flat roofs.
solar_partial: only {n} of {total} fit on the face
solar_form_hint: Modules that would reach beyond the roof face are left out. “Fill face” puts as many modules on the roof as fit. kWp counted with 400 W per module.
chimney_hint: The height counts from the upper side, where the chimney leaves the roof. Drag it in the plan or in the 3D view, also onto another roof face.
roof_windows_hint: Roof windows lie in the roof face, with a blind and contacts like windows. Drag them in the plan, also onto another roof face.
roof_window_motor_hint: A window motor (Velux, Roto, Fakro) reports its position as a cover: the sash opens in 3D as far as the motor stands. A contact or tilt contact still works without a motor.
roof_window_hint: Open, the sash swings out, hinged at the top; tilted, a little; and the frame glows warm; the blind comes down over the glass from the top. In a roof section the window cuts a hole into the slope, so the attic looks out through it.
solar_tilt_wall: Tilt away from the wall (°, 90 = canopy)
solar_flip_wall: Standing off at the bottom instead of the top
inverter_strings_none: No string on this inverter yet – assign it at a solar field under String › Inverter.
solar_string_inverter_missing: No inverter in the plan yet (add one below under Devices)
solar_string_hint: Fields in the same string belong together, also on different roofs (e.g. 5 modules on the house and 5 on the garage). Sensor and inverter count for the whole string.
solar_face_size: Roof face {w} × {h} m (along the eave × up the slope)
solar_cols_hint: One number for rows of equal length, or a list for rows of their own: “4, 4, 3” (from the eave).
solar_pick_hint: Tap a module in the plan to take it away or put it back. Removed ones are dashed.
solar_entity: PV power of this field (e.g. its string)
grid_point_hint: The grid connection stands here: the handover point to the utility, e.g. at the end of the driveway. Movable in the plan.
furn_tap_hint: An own action like the star menu's own buttons, e.g. a browser_mod popup with your card.
furn_show_when_invert: The other way round: show while it is not
furn_show_when_hint: Seasonal decoration that only stands in December: a helper (input_boolean), a calendar or a sensor decides whether the piece shows in 3D. Separate several states with commas. The editor always shows it.
picture_hint: Your photo in the frame, in 3D and on the wall tablet. Uploaded photos are stored with the plan in a smaller size; an image entity (a photo of the day) or a camera shows its current picture.
furn_state_hint: The item glows while the entity reports on, occupied or home – a bed with an occupancy mat, an armchair, the sauna. Two entities light the halves: left and right, bottom and top for a bunk bed.
fix_hint: Fixed: cannot be moved by accident any more (key L, right-click or long press)
fixed_drag_hint: 🔒 Fixed – release it first to move it (lock in the form, right-click or key L)
fixed_delete_confirm: This item is fixed. Delete it anyway?
lock_plan_hint: Lock the floor plan: rooms, walls, doors, windows and outdoor areas cannot be moved by accident. Furniture and devices stay free.
start_view_hint: The 3D view, the card and the kiosk open the house with this view, e.g. from the garden side. Turn, zoom and move the house in the 3D pane on the right until it fits, then remember it.
start_view_card: If a card should open with a different view, put this line into its YAML configuration.
start_view_set: Remember the current 3D view as the start
start_view_saved: An own start view is saved.
climate_hint: These sensors count for the heatmap and the room panel. “Automatic” takes the sensors of the area and the ones placed in the room, but no device temperatures (3D printer, heat pump, flow …).
opening_mark_hint: A highlighted window or door glows warm. “When closed” needs a contact; without a sensor nothing is highlighted.
window_opens_hint: Sliding: the pane on the hinge side slides in front of the fixed one; with two leaves the middle two slide outwards. Top-hung windows open with their contact or a tilt sensor.
marker_show_hint: Automatic follows the None / Important / All switch of the 3D view. Always show and Hide apply regardless (except with None).
pin_shift_hint: When devices stand close together, push the pin a little aside or up here (in metres); the device itself stays where it is.
show_name: Show the name under the marker in 3D
card_marker_names_hint: Every device with an own name shows it small under its marker – three thermometers in the garden stay apart.
card_tap_in_room: Switch devices only in the opened room
card_tap_in_room_hint: In the house and floor views a tap opens the floor or room, even on a device or its marker. In the opened room it switches the device. A long press always opens its menu or details.
card_markers_outside: Choose the markers outside the opened room
card_markers_outside_hint: In the house, on the floor and in the other rooms only the ticked kinds; in the opened room all, as set above. A device's own "always" and "never" come first.
device_name_hint: A name for the plan and the room panel only, e.g. "Island accent light" – the entity in Server_Monits stays as it is.
device_simple: Switch only in the room panel
device_simple_hint: The room panel shows only the switch for this lamp, without brightness, colour temperature and colours.
floor_shift_all_hint: Shift and turn act on every floor with the roof sections, outdoor areas, energy devices and meter – the whole house moves as one.
floor_turn_hint: Turns everything on the floor by 90° clockwise about the middle of its rooms – when a floor was drawn the wrong way round. Three times = 270°.
marker_icon_hint: The name of a Material Design icon as in Server_Monits, e.g. mdi:thermometer or mdi:water-alert. Empty = the symbol of the device kind.
furn_links_hint: With a power sensor the item shows its watts and takes part in the energy flow.
furn_links_hint_tv: The screen glows while the TV is on, in the colour of the app (Netflix, YouTube …); the label shows the app or title.
stairs_hint: The stair rises towards the back (away from the marked front edge) and opens the ceiling of the floor above.
stair_landing_hint: The landing lies {h} cm above the floor; the other risers come after it.
stair_down_hint: The stair starts on this floor and leads down, for example into a cellar that need not be drawn. It opens the floor of this level.
stair_measures: {steps} risers of {rise} cm · going {going} cm · step measure {measure} cm
stair_uncomfortable: uncomfortable (step measure 59–65 cm, rise at most 21 cm)
stair_up_note: The stair starts at the marked front edge. The floor above opens only where less than 2.2 m of headroom is left above the steps.
stair_down_note: You step onto the stair at the marked front edge and walk down. The plan draws it dashed; this floor opens above the steps.
stair_opening_hint: How much of the floor the stair reaches it opens: the floor above, or its own floor for a stair going down. By headroom opens only above the steps that lack 2.2 m.
stair_up_note_plain: The stair starts at the marked front edge and rises towards the back.
stair_upgrade_hint: Turns this into a stair with a shape (winding, L, U, spiral), build, railing and number of steps.
energy_meters_hint: Gas and water show with the house's balance – in the energy bar and on the house card: a sensor with the flow now (m³/h, l/min) or today's reading.
energy_hint: Consumers are placed devices with a power sensor (W) – the sensor itself or one of the same device.
energy_balance_hint: Grid, solar and battery come from the devices in the plan: meter, inverter and home battery. Here you can choose other sensors, flip signs and set the house consumption.
energy_show_unmetered_hint: A sub-meter's label then shows what its floors use and how much of it no placed device measures, e.g. “500 W · 450 W unmetered”. Otherwise it shows the meter's reading.
energy_advanced_hint: For sub-meters, e.g. one per flat behind a main meter: a meter can then hang off another one and feed its own floors. Off = the first meter is the grid connection, further ones are consumers.
energy_consumption_sensor: House consumption (W, else from the balance)
energy_import_prefs: Take over from the energy dashboard
energy_import_done: {n} sensors taken over – please check the signs.
energy_import_none: No matching power sensors (W) were found in the energy dashboard – please choose them by hand.
energy_import_failed: Server_Monits' energy dashboard is not set up.
hint_meter: Tap the spot of the meter
ble_hint: Locate a Bluetooth tag (key fob, watch, phone) by room: walk through the rooms with it and record each room. NextFloor then compares how strongly Server_Monits' Bluetooth scanners (ESPHome proxies, Shelly devices with Bluetooth switched on, adapters on the server) hear it. Every tag gets a sensor whose state is the room name.
ble_unavailable: Server_Monits' Bluetooth integration is not running. Without it there are no scanners.
ble_scanners: {n} Bluetooth scanners in Server_Monits. The more scanners in different rooms, the more exact.
ble_none_heard: No scanner hears the tag right now. Hold it near a scanner and wait a moment; a tag only sends every few seconds.
ble_no_address: This phone or watch has no known address right now. Check Server_Monits' Private BLE Device integration.
ble_one_scanner: Only one scanner hears the tag. Telling rooms apart takes at least two, better three or more.
ble_learn_hint: Pick the room, press Record and walk slowly through the whole room with the tag in your hand, into the corners too. Recording again replaces the room. Learn every room you want to locate the tag in.
ble_sensor_hint: The sensor "{name}" (device NextFloor) shows the room. Under Presence you can pick it as a person's room sensor.
presence_hint: Room sensor per person (e.g. ESPresense, Bermuda): its state names the room or area.
no_persons: There are no people in Server_Monits.
